desc:
The string s consists only of the letters a, b and c. Return the number of substrings that contain at least one a, at least one b and at least one c.

Substrings are counted by position.

s = "abcabc"
abc, abca, abcab, abcabc, bca, bcab, bcabc, cab, cabc, abc
result = 10
constraints: s contains only the letters a, b and c
hints: Count by right end. If a substring ending at right already contains all three letters, what happens when you extend it to the left?
Extending to the left keeps all three letters, so for each right end the valid starts are a prefix 0..t of the possible starts (not a suffix as in the "at most" problems).
t is the smallest of the last positions of a, b and c seen so far. Equivalently: total substrings minus those with at most 2 distinct letters.
editorial: Fix the right end r. Let la, lb, lc be the most recent indices (at or before r) of each letter. A substring [i, r] has all three letters iff i ≤ min(la, lb, lc), so there are min(la, lb, lc) + 1 valid starts once all three letters have appeared (and none before that).

Summing over all right ends gives the answer in a single pass with O(1) memory. Equivalently, substrings with all three letters = all substrings minus substrings with at most 2 distinct letters, which is the "at most k distinct" window count with k = 2; the two views give the same number. Time O(n), space O(1).
solution:
def countAllThree(s):
    last = [-1, -1, -1]
    total = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        last[ord(ch) - 97] = i
        total += min(last) + 1
    return total
